name: Mushi
title: Son of Merari and head of the Levitical clan
summary: Mushi was a son of Merari, who was a son of Levi. He founded the Mushite clan, one of the Levitical families assigned specific duties related to the service of the tabernacle. The Mushites were responsible for carrying parts of the tabernacle's structure during the wilderness journey.

keyEvents.title: The lineage of Mushi is mentioned
keyEvents.description: Mushi is mentioned as the son of Merari and grandson of Levi in Israel's genealogical records.

keyEvents.title: The Mushite clan is counted
keyEvents.description: During the census in the wilderness, the Mushite clan was counted among the descendants of Merari who served at the tabernacle.

keyEvents.title: The Duties of the Mushiites at the Tabernacle
keyEvents.description: The Mushiites were assigned to carry specific parts of the tabernacle's structure, including planks, crossbars, pillars, and bases.

keyEvents.title: Mushi in the Genealogical Records of Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Mushi is mentioned in the detailed genealogy in 1 Chronicles as a son of Merari.

keyEvents.title: The Descendants of Mushi Are Mentioned
keyEvents.description: In 1 Chronicles, further information is given about the sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth.

keyEvents.title: The Division of Levitical Service under David
keyEvents.description: During King David's organization of the Levitical service, the clan of the Mushiites was assigned specific roles in temple worship.
